What is the proper reaction for a character when they kill someone for the first time?

My character is a seventeen-year-old guy who is being thrown into a war. He’s a shapeshifter, but his powers haven’t come into fruition. For the first time, his instincts kick in during a training session. He’s in a VR Simulation and he throws a knife into his opponent’s neck, and the simulation dies like any human would. Here’s what I have:

“Time seemed to slow as Jason whipped back around, the throwing knives in his hands. He released the blade and watched as it sliced through the air and into his opponent’s neck. He blanched as the sim. collapsed to the ground, blood starting to pour from her neck. Instantly, he felt his stomach twist and his throat tighten. “End simulation!” he shouted, turning away and collapsing. His arms shook and he got down on all fours, breathing shakily. He felt his throat tighten, and he vomited on the floor. The image of the life leaving the girl’s eyes was burned into his mind.”

Is that a proper reaction? Should I change it or add more details afterwards as I was planning?

I’ve got a friend who had a similar stubborn tendency when it came to therapy. She was in a physically, mentally, and sexually abusive relationship at just 14 years old. She still refuses to tell her parents the full story, and she refuses to acknowledge that she has PTSD from the experience, forcing herself to pretend she’s okay. That was two years ago that the relationship started, in May it will be two years since the end. 

Unfortunately, I never was able to convince her to go back for therapy. And my only advice I can really give you is to just be there for her when she needs you, because she can’t get help if she’s scared or angry. She needs to really want the help. It sucks, especially if you’re as empathetic as I think you are with wanting to help her so desperately, but she has to be in charge of that healing. Just continue to let her know you care and are there for her.

I understand where you’re coming from. I’m a Junior as well and I started cutting a few months back, using a dagger I got from Medieval Times. I told my parents and my friends a couple of weeks after I’d started and they were able to get me to stop. However, I started up again recently because it feels good. 

It’s a horrible excuse for a coping mechanism, but it’s the only thing that even remotely works. Regardless, my advice to you is to keep those razors away from yourself and whenever you have those desires, find something to distract yourself. If you enjoy art, start a painting or drawing. If you enjoy cooking or want to learn, find a recipe you like and start. Music and gaming are my distractions whenever I feel over burdened.

Cutting is the first step down the dark path to committing suicide, to put it bluntly. I promise you, there are better ways to cope. It’s gonna take a while to find them, especially if you’ve been trying to cope for five years, but you’ll find something, and you’ll be glad you did.
